title: Generate Numeric Range via Recursive CTE
description_markdown: Use a recursive CTE named `numbers` to generate a series of integers from 1 to 5. Return `num`. Order by `num` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive CTE syntax
WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (
  SELECT 1 AS num -- anchor
  UNION ALL
  SELECT num + 1 FROM numbers WHERE num < 5 -- recursive
)
SELECT num FROM numbers ORDER BY num ASC;
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (SELECT 1 AS num UNION ALL SELECT num + 1 FROM numbers WHERE num < 5) SELECT num FROM numbers ORDER BY num ASC;
solution_explanation: A recursive CTE consists of an anchor member, UNION ALL, and a recursive term referencing the CTE name.
hints: Use `WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (SELECT 1 AS num UNION ALL SELECT num + 1 FROM numbers WHERE num < 5)`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (SELECT 1 AS num UNION ALL SELECT num + 1 FROM numbers WHERE num < 5) SELECT num FROM numbers ORDER BY num ASC;

title: Traverse Category Tree and Build Breadcrumb Paths

Calculate `level` (starting at 1) and concatenate `path` as `TEXT` (`category_name` for root, and `path || ' > ' || category_name` for children). Return `category_id`, `category_name`, and `level`. Order by `level` ASC, `category_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive hierarchy traversal
WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (
  ...
)
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 1 AS level FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ct.level + 1 FROM categories c JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id) SELECT category_id, category_name, level FROM category_tree ORDER BY level ASC, category_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Traverses self-referential tree relations by connecting recursive terms to parents.
hints: Anchor: `SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 1 AS level FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL`.
Recursive member: `JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 1 AS level FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ct.level + 1 FROM categories c JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id) SELECT category_id, category_name, level FROM category_tree ORDER BY level ASC, category_id ASC;

  ...

)

solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE countdown AS (SELECT 10 AS val UNION ALL SELECT val - 1 FROM countdown WHERE val > 1) SELECT val FROM countdown ORDER BY val DESC;

interview_tip: Recursive queries can decrement values as easily as incrementing them.

Subtract 1 while `val > 1`.
Query: WITH RECURSIVE countdown AS (SELECT 10 AS val UNION ALL SELECT val - 1 FROM countdown WHERE val > 1) SELECT val FROM countdown ORDER BY val DESC;

title: Compute Running Triangular Sums
description_markdown: Use a recursive CTE named `triangular` starting with `step = 1` and `running_sum = 1`. In each recursive step, increase `step` by 1 and add the new step to `running_sum` up to `step = 5`. Return `step` and `running_sum`. Order by `step` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Triangular numbers running sum
WITH RECURSIVE triangular AS (
  SELECT 1 AS step, 1 AS running_sum
  UNION ALL
  SELECT step + 1, running_sum + (step + 1) FROM triangular WHERE step < 5
)
SELECT step, running_sum FROM triangular ORDER BY step ASC;
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE triangular AS (SELECT 1 AS step, 1 AS running_sum UNION ALL SELECT step + 1, running_sum + (step + 1) FROM triangular WHERE step < 5) SELECT step, running_sum FROM triangular ORDER BY step ASC;
solution_explanation: Accumulates triangular numbers: (1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 6), (4, 10), (5, 15).
common_mistakes: Adding old step instead of new step.
interview_tip: Maintaining multiple state columns in recursive CTEs allows calculating accumulators without window functions.
hints: Anchor: `SELECT 1 AS step, 1 AS running_sum`.
Recursion: `SELECT step + 1, running_sum + (step + 1) FROM triangular WHERE step < 5`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE triangular AS (SELECT 1 AS step, 1 AS running_sum UNION ALL SELECT step + 1, running_sum + (step + 1) FROM triangular WHERE step < 5) SELECT step, running_sum FROM triangular ORDER BY step ASC;

title: Generate First 7 Fibonacci Terms
description_markdown: Use a recursive CTE named `fib` with anchor `n = 1`, `a = 0`, `b = 1` (where `b` is the current Fibonacci value). In each recursive step up to `n < 7`, set `n = n + 1`, new `a = b`, and new `b = a + b`. Return `n` as `term` and `b` as `fib_val`. Order by `term` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Fibonacci series
WITH RECURSIVE fib AS (
  SELECT 1 AS n, 0 AS a, 1 AS b
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n + 1, b, a + b FROM fib WHERE n < 7
)
SELECT n AS term, b AS fib_val FROM fib ORDER BY term ASC;
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE fib AS (SELECT 1 AS n, 0 AS a, 1 AS b UNION ALL SELECT n + 1, b, a + b FROM fib WHERE n < 7) SELECT n AS term, b AS fib_val FROM fib ORDER BY term ASC;
solution_explanation: Two state variables a and b track previous two Fibonacci numbers across iterations.
common_mistakes: Failing to advance both state variables simultaneously in the projection.
interview_tip: State tuple passing (a, b) -> (b, a + b) is the standard recurrence relation pattern in SQL.
hints: Anchor: `SELECT 1 AS n, 0 AS a, 1 AS b`.
Recursive step: `SELECT n + 1, b, a + b FROM fib WHERE n < 7`.
Query: WITH RECURSIVE fib AS (SELECT 1 AS n, 0 AS a, 1 AS b UNION ALL SELECT n + 1, b, a + b FROM fib WHERE n < 7) SELECT n AS term, b AS fib_val FROM fib ORDER BY term ASC;

title: Traverse Subordinates of Engineering VP
description_markdown: Using a recursive CTE `subordinates`, anchor on the employee where `job_title = 'VP of Engineering'` at `level = 1`. Recursively find all employees reporting directly or indirectly to them (`e.manager_id = s.emp_id`), incrementing `level` by 1. Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, and `level`. starter_query:
-- Subordinates of VP of Engineering
WITH RECURSIVE subordinates AS (
  SELECT emp_id, first_name, manager_id, 1 AS level
  FROM employees
  WHERE job_title = 'VP of Engineering'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.manager_id, s.level + 1
  FROM employees e
  JOIN subordinates s ON e.manager_id = s.emp_id
)
SELECT emp_id, first_name, level
FROM subordinates
ORDER BY level ASC, emp_id ASC;

common_mistakes: Joining on e.emp_id = s.manager_id which traverses upwards instead of downwards.
interview_tip: To traverse downward: JOIN on employee.manager_id = recursive_result.emp_id.
hints: Anchor: `SELECT emp_id, first_name, manager_id, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE job_title = 'VP of Engineering'`.
Recursive join: `JOIN subordinates s ON e.manager_id = s.emp_id`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE subordinates AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, manager_id, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE job_title = 'VP of Engineering' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.manager_id, s.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN subordinates s ON e.manager_id = s.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, level FROM subordinates ORDER BY level ASC, emp_id ASC;
